findings.summary: C2 counts BSD `-J <s>` as an xargs replace option, but today's skipXargs does not know -J takes an argument, and no worked-example line pins it. A task can do the replace string for -I, -i and --replace only, pass every gate, and leave `xargs -J % git push` allowed. That command runs git push and is allowed today. BSD -R and -S also take an argument that skipXargs does not skip, so `xargs -I {} -R 1 git push` and `xargs -S 255 -I {} git push` read `1` or `255` as the command name and are allowed. This is the same bypass: a word before the name that the judge misreads.
findings.evidence: internal/fence/judge.go skipXargs: only the letters "adEILnPs" take an argument. `man xargs` on macOS lists -J replstr, -R replacements and -S replsize. On the base binary, review phase: `echo x | xargs -J % git push origin` => allow; `echo x | xargs -I {} -R 1 git push` => allow; `echo x | xargs -S 255 -I {} git push` => allow.
findings.fix: Add `review  echo x | xargs -J % git push   → deny: git push is denied by the review fence (Bash(git push:*))` under # C2, and say in C2's xargs bullet that -J, -R and -S take an argument (name skipXargs's letter table in the judge.go reference). If -R/-S are not wanted here, name them in Out of scope instead.

findings.summary: The hook bullet in fence-audit lists what the judge denies ('… a command word starting with `$`'). C4 adds only what B35 reads and the any-text matching, not the three refusals B35 adds: a command word that expands anywhere, an expanded word before the command name (or before a shell's -c string), and a redirection target holding a glob or a brace expansion. After the run the audit understates the hook's refusals. configuration.md's new text leaves out the same three.
findings.evidence: docs/design-notes/fence-audit.md:22-25 ('What it cannot parse it denies: … a command word starting with `$`.'). C2 introduces 'command word <word> expands…', '<word> expands before the command name…', 'a redirection target that expands cannot be resolved: …'. C4's texts for both docs mention none of them.
findings.fix: Extend the C4 sentence added to the hook bullet with: 'and refuses a command word, a word before it, or a redirection target that expands (B35)'. Add the same clause to the configuration.md replacement.

decisions: Drop the leading keyword and judge the rest, rather than parsing the grammar (no mvdan.cc/sh). Agree: nothing runs that is not judged as its own command.
case, select, function, coproc, [[ and function definitions stay refused. Agree: none appears in the counted denials.

An expanded word ($, glob, brace) matches as any text and is not resolved. This is the main trade-off: it denies common harmless calls (git diff "$BASE", git show "$SHA", find "$d", and in work sessions rm "$f" and rm *.tmp). Agree: it closes real bypasses, confirmed on the base binary (`X=push; git $X origin`, `g$X push origin`, `nice -n $N push origin`, `bash -$O -c …` are all allowed today).
A command name that expands anywhere is refused, as is an expanded word a wrapper skips or a shell option before -c. Agree.
A redirection target holding a glob or a brace expansion is refused. Agree.
xargs is matched as if it ended with an expanded word, and the replace string counts as expanded. Agree; see finding 1 for -J/-R/-S.
command -v/-V (literal option) runs nothing; time -v does not. Agree.
Subshells are read; `((` is refused as arithmetic; other arithmetic contexts (let, ${a[x]}, declare -i) are left for a later brief. Acceptable; they are named in Out of scope.
A keyword after a wrapper is not dropped (env ! x stays denied). Agree.
C2 applies in every phase. Agree.
